_comment: Outcome measurement and paper trading. method_version changes whenever the outcome semantics change (milestone 5 adds the tracker coverage check and the week report WITHOUT changing them: m1.0 stays). community_gate holds the frozen go/no-go criteria for community alerts that `fart measure week` tests and prints; it decides nothing and sends nothing.

paper._comment: entry/exit fee come from config/pumpfun.json total_curve_fee_bps (curve math); the *_fee_bps here are informational

tracker._comment: Tracker fidelity (milestone 5, point 4): a graduation counts as tracker-covered when its mcap_samples rows in the winner window are never more than max_sample_gap_s apart (the tracker runs every 300 s; 600 s allows one missed run). A graduation whose stored outcome says 'no winner' but that is NOT tracker-covered is reported as 'uitkomst onbekend' (a peak between sparse samples may have been missed), never as 'geen winnaar'. A graduation that IS a winner stays a winner (sparse samples cannot invent a peak). The outcomes rows themselves are unchanged (method_version m1.0).

week._comment: fart measure week: a rolling window of `days` UTC days ending at --end (default yesterday), written to out/recall/week-<end>.md|json. The Monday 06:30 UTC run covers the whole Monday-Sunday calendar week. Confidence intervals: block bootstrap with days as blocks (a NIET GEDEKT day is not a block and never counts as a day with zero winners), `draws` draws, fixed `seed`, two-sided `alpha`; with fewer than min_days covered days or fewer than min_winners winners the report says 'te weinig data' instead of an interval.

community_gate._comment: Go/no-go criteria for community alerts, frozen BEFORE the measurement week (docs/DECISIONS.md, milestone 5, 26 Oct 2026). Start values chosen by the builder; Jim may adjust them before the week ends, never afterwards. The week report prints every criterion as voldaan / niet voldaan / te weinig data and an overall verdict; nothing is decided or sent by it. complete day = a day of the window in which every peak hour (peak_hours_utc, 12:00-02:00 UTC as the hours 12..23 and 0..1 of that UTC day) was covered. hit rate = observe (coin) decisions that became a winner within 24 h, over the decisions whose 24 h have elapsed: an unknown outcome stays in the denominator (not a demonstrated hit), a pending one is listed apart. recall = winners with an observe or observe_meta decision before graduation. lead time = graduation minus the earliest observe/observe_meta decision. observations per day = observe + observe_meta decisions per covered day. frozen_rules: the rules_version that started the measurement week and the fingerprint of the rule-defining files at that commit (fart/version.py RULE_FILES); every later rules_version with the same fingerprint ran the same rules and is pooled with it. frozen_rules_equivalents (milestone 11): fingerprints of later commits whose rule files provably compute exactly what the frozen rules compute (same metas, features and verdicts on a fixture database, proven by the named test); the week report pools them with frozen_rules and names them under the segment title, the website calls them frozen. An entry is added only together with its proof and its DECISIONS.md entry; a real rules change never goes here.

frozen_rules_equivalents.note: Milestone 11: the meta baseline (the coins of 6 to 48 h before as_of) is fetched and tokenized once per tick instead of once per term (590 to 598 s per tick on the VPS on 29 Oct 2026). Same rules, same outcomes: the test runs the frozen old implementation (tests/frozen/) next to the new one on a fixture database of at least 20,000 coins over 48 h and 50,000 trades and proves byte-equal metas, coin features and verdicts. Only the computation time changed; the week report pools this fingerprint with frozen_rules and says so under the segment title.
